text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey's coalition government is heavily subsidising farmers in an effort to win votes, while not giving the armed forces money to pay for their campaign in northern Iraq.
- While the government's conservative wing has agreed to help its Islamist partners fight off a prosecution, disagreement on issues connected with a possible early election continues.
- Opposition politicians heavily criticised the government's failure to pay the armed forces for their campaign in northern Iraq.
- The armed forces are calling for a boycott of goods of companies thought to be backing Islamist activities.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told a closed party meeting the army are looking for excuses for their own lack of military success against rebel Kurds by attacking the Islamist-led government.
- President Suleyman Demirel will present the Iranian president with a dossier detailing alleged links between Iran and Kurdish rebels fighting in Turkey's troubled southeast.
- Tension between the armed forces over payment for the army's Iraq campaign has ended with agreement between Erbakan and the generals.
- Left-wing politician, Fikri Saglar, has said that a farm owned by deputy prime minister, Tansu Ciller, was used as a transit point in the trafficking of drugs.
